decisions.reason: As a supplement line close to the existing consumer-health offer and publicly presented on its own page, it fits the firm's announced portfolio-broadening strategy and management is likely to continue rather than admit a failed launch.

This product was visibly launched with explicit marketing language and sits squarely in the firm's established supplement business, so sunk commercial effort and strategic fit make continuation more likely than withdrawal.

After being introduced and then upgraded to its own page, this joint-health supplement shows enough public commitment within the core portfolio that management would tend to persist unless failure were unmistakable.

The firm promoted this immune supplement as an innovative addition and made it part of the Trivital line, so the visible commitment and relevance to consumer-health expansion support keeping it on the market.

Although more distant from the established offer and affected by a reported problem, a generic prescription medicine carries meaningful regulatory and launch investment and the setback can be framed as temporary, which favors persistence.

This OTC migraine product is somewhat outside the firm's usual range, but as a recent launch in a regulated category tied to portfolio expansion, management is likely to give it more time rather than write off the investment quickly.
